name: memory-firewall-dashboard
description: Forensic lab UI for Memory Firewall: ingest and scan, source trust map, memory ledger, quarantine review, claim conflicts, retrieval trace, time machine and attack lab.
comment: This dashboard has ZERO runtime dependencies and no bundler. Sources are TypeScript compiled
to native ES modules, which the browser loads directly. The consequences are deliberate:
the production image is a static file server, there is no transitive dependency surface in a
security tool's own UI, and the build cannot break because of a toolchain upgrade.
docs/DECISIONS.md records why this was chosen over React/Vite/Tailwind and what it costs.
NO package-lock.json is committed: the environment this was built in could not reach the npm
registry, so one could not be generated, and hand-writing integrity hashes would be worse than
shipping none. The single devDependency is pinned to an EXACT version, so `npm install` is
reproducible in practice. Run `npm install` once with network access and commit the resulting
lockfile to make it reproducible by construction.
